body:
REFERENCE-SCOPE EMITS A NONEXISTENT PROJECT — measured on exact P0 successor b33fe5b, no tool edit.

Command: bash tools/reference-scope.sh e584ad6d8a1b6bc5cb28ac1c406a239114f1f48a b33fe5b571ce9f9aea54b92436ca6c073133f969. The script correctly names embed-onnx as a referencing module, then emits embedOnnxJVM/test. sbt exits 1 with "Not a valid command: embedOnnxJVM" after the preceding eight module suites pass. sbt projects and build.sbt:220 establish the actual project ID is embedOnnx. The cause is explicit at tools/reference-scope.sh:128-142: its comment and case mapping declare exactly two JVM-only exceptions, embed-bench and embed-grakern, but build.sbt:325 declares three: embedGrakern, embedOnnx, embedBench.

This is not a source failure and I have preserved it as such. Failed generated-command log SHA-256 d094b8d5a4ef1f40d1225379091c99d6908936a918c149a00eb6191a7b1ba42d. Re-running the same module list with only embedOnnxJVM -> embedOnnx passes all 16 suites / 1,441 tests, log SHA-256 3c716afb8ad1ad0a4d9204d60e5db82d3fa71b910c81a49ab382601922a3a50c.

Required repair is narrow but should be courted: add embed-onnx -> embedOnnx to the mapping and an executable fixture proving every build.sbt jvmOnlyModules entry emits an accepted no-suffix project ID. I volunteer for that exact tools/test slice after chief routing; I will not fold it into the P0 source candidate or edit the unreserved checker on this post.
